Everything PulseZones can do

Bluetooth heart rate tracking,
zone alerts and workout reports

Connect your heart rate strap, monitor your workout and share your progress. Here is what PulseZones can do on Android.

Which Bluetooth chest straps work with PulseZones?

Connect a compatible Bluetooth Low Energy sensor directly in PulseZones. The developer has personally tested the GEOID HS500, Magene H303 and Magene H603. Other models need to support the standard Bluetooth Heart Rate Service.

Can I see live heart rate from my chest strap on Android?

Follow your current heart rate, zone number and chart during your session. The home screen also shows the connected sensor and its battery status.

How can I track time in heart rate zones?

Five color-coded zones show your workout intensity. Follow your current zone and the time spent in each zone as your workout progresses.

Does the app have heart rate zone alerts?

Yes. Choose a target zone and get an alert when you leave it, or enable alerts whenever you move between zones. Sound and vibration let you follow your effort without looking at your phone.

Can I use Karvonen heart rate reserve zones?

Choose the Karvonen method and enter your resting heart rate. The standard method uses percentages of maximum heart rate. Set your maximum manually or use an age-based estimate.

Learn about the calculation methods →

Can I track GPS routes, running pace and cycling speed?

Enable GPS recording to track your route, distance, duration, speed and pace. Choose kilometers or miles and switch between the map and heart rate chart during your workout.

Does heart rate recording work in the background?

PulseZones keeps recording an active workout in the background. Heart rate, pace and distance are available in the system notification, including on the lock screen.

Where can I see my workout history and heart rate charts?

Open a saved session in your history to see duration, distance, average and maximum heart rate, the chart, time in zones and your recorded route in one report.

How do I share my workout results?

Open a saved workout and use Share to send the report to your coach, friends or training group.

Can I see weekly and monthly training statistics?

Choose a period and activity type to see your workout count, total distance and duration, average heart rate, daily distance and time in each heart rate zone.

How do I share weekly or monthly training statistics?

Select a week or month in Statistics and share the summary report. It is a convenient way to show your training volume and intensity distribution for the whole period.

Which app supports running, cycling and strength training?

PulseZones includes running, cycling, hiking, strength, cardio, sport and sleep modes, plus a demo mode. Choose a mode for your session and review statistics by activity type.

Is PulseZones a free heart rate monitor app with no ads?

Yes. There are no ads, subscriptions or mandatory sign-ups. You need a compatible Bluetooth heart rate sensor: PulseZones reads the sensor's data rather than measuring your pulse with the phone camera.

Can I record heart rate and workouts offline?

Core PulseZones features work offline. Your profile, workout history and routes are stored locally on your smartphone.

Which languages does the heart rate monitor app support?

PulseZones supports ten languages: English, Russian, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, German, French, Italian, Polish, Turkish and Georgian.

How can I make heart rate readings easier to read?

Adjust the text size in the app to make workout metrics easier to read.

Where does the app get its heart rate data?

PulseZones displays readings transmitted by the connected sensor. It does not invent heart rate values or replace them with calculated estimates. Measurement accuracy depends on the sensor, skin contact and connection quality.

How does the app process GPS routes?

Coordinates come from your phone's location system. PulseZones smooths suspicious jumps and processes the track before saving to reduce the effects of GPS errors. Processing cannot replace a good signal: route quality still depends on your phone and reception conditions.

Compatibility

Connect your Bluetooth heart rate monitor to Android

PulseZones works with BLE sensors that transmit heart rate using the standard Bluetooth Heart Rate Service.

1

Put on and activate your sensor

Moisten the strap electrodes and secure the strap around your chest. Most sensors turn on automatically.

2

Open PulseZones

Allow Bluetooth and nearby device access, then select your sensor in the app.

3

Start your workout

Choose an activity and tap Start. After your session, disconnect the sensor and remember to take it off. We also recommend detaching the sensor from the strap.

Tested models: GEOID HS500, Magene H303 and Magene H603. Other models may also work if they support the standard BLE Heart Rate Service.

Before your first workout

Android permissions
for Bluetooth and background recording

Check Permissions and background operation in PulseZones settings. It helps you prepare your phone for stable operation during workouts, including with the screen off.

Nearby devices: connect your Bluetooth sensor

Allow nearby device discovery and connection so PulseZones can find your heart rate monitor and receive its data. Bluetooth must also be enabled on your phone. The permission name and whether a separate prompt appears depend on your Android version.

Precise location: record your route

Allow precise location while using the app and turn on your phone's location services to record GPS routes, distance, speed and pace. The app requests this permission when you enable route recording. Heart rate recording still works without it.

Notifications: view your workout in the background

Allow PulseZones notifications to see your current heart rate, available pace or speed during GPS recording, and sensor connection status when the app is minimised or your screen is off.

Unrestricted battery use: keep long workouts recording

Allow PulseZones to run without battery restrictions. Power-saving settings may limit background operation, disconnect the sensor or stop recording. Find PulseZones in your battery settings and choose Unrestricted, Don't optimise or the equivalent option.

Lock screen: check metrics without unlocking

Allow PulseZones notifications on the lock screen. If Live heart rate, Sensor connection and Workout route are separate categories, check each one. Whether notification contents are visible also depends on your lock-screen privacy settings.

Autostart: if your phone offers this setting

Some manufacturers apply additional limits to app startup and background operation. If your system has an autostart setting, allow it for PulseZones. Not having this option does not, by itself, mean anything is wrong.

Why does PulseZones still show a battery optimization warning?

On some phones, allowing background operation and exempting an app from battery optimisation are separate settings. PulseZones checks whether Android confirms the optimisation exemption. The warning may therefore remain even after background operation is allowed.

Find Battery optimisation in system settings, choose All apps if necessary, then select PulseZones. Check what the switch actually controls: Don't allow may refer to disallowing battery optimisation, rather than preventing the app from running.

Settings vary between phones. Names, menu paths and available switches depend on the manufacturer, model, Android version and system interface. Check the manufacturer's manual or support pages. If you cannot find an option, search online using your exact model, for example: '[model] allow app background activity', '[model] disable battery optimisation for app' or '[model] lock screen notifications'. Include your system version, because menus can change after an update.

How do I check that recording continues with the screen off?

Connect your sensor, start a short workout and turn the screen off for a few minutes. Then check that heart rate recording and, if GPS is enabled, route recording continued. A trial session helps reveal restrictions on your particular phone.

Why train with heart rate zones?

Heart rate zone training: match your effort to your goal

Heart rate indicates how hard your body is working. Zones turn beats per minute into a useful guide to recovery, easy aerobic work, tempo efforts and high intensity.

They help you avoid starting too fast, maintain a chosen effort and compare similar sessions. Zone boundaries are approximate and depend on the calculation method.

Why zones matterCompare calculation methods
Zone 590–100%Maximum intensity
Zone 480–89%High intensity
Zone 370–79%Moderately hard
Zone 260–69%Aerobic training
Zone 150–59%Light effort

Train with purpose

Heart rate zones for easy runs and interval workouts

It is easy to get carried away on a run: start a little faster, push up a hill or catch another runner. A planned easy session quietly becomes a hard one. Heart rate zones help you notice the change and maintain the effort you intended.

A zone is a range of heart rates. PulseZones uses five, from light effort to high intensity. They help you understand not just how long you trained, but how demanding the session was.

Use heart rate to keep easy runs easy

When the goal is to accumulate training volume, speed is not always the priority. It matters more to complete the session at a suitable intensity and leave enough energy for your next workouts.

Monitoring heart rate helps you avoid speeding up without noticing. This is especially useful on long runs, in hot weather or on hilly routes: the same pace can require very different effort in different conditions. Sometimes slowing down is the sensible way to maintain your intended intensity.

Check your breathing too: at moderate intensity, you can usually speak in sentences. If talking becomes difficult, your effort is already substantially higher.

Follow effort and recovery during interval training

During interval training, harder repetitions alternate with easier recovery periods. The heart rate chart helps you see how your body responds, while time in zones lets you review the overall intensity distribution afterwards.

Heart rate responds with a delay. During a short acceleration, it may only rise near the end, then stay elevated for a while after you slow down. Use duration, pace and perceived effort to guide intervals too. Do not push harder just to reach a particular colour on the screen.

Look at the whole workout afterwards

The same 40 minutes could be an easy run, a tempo session or a set of intervals. Time in each zone helps you tell the difference.

PulseZones lets you follow your current zone, view your heart rate chart and revisit your results after the finish. Compare the plan with what actually happened: did the easy run stay easy, and did hard intervals alternate with recovery?

Heart rate zones are a guide, not a good-or-bad score. A useful effort is one that matches your workout's purpose and how you feel.

Sources: CDC — intensity and the talk test; Suunto — heart rate during intervals.

How to choose a zone calculation method →

Understanding the calculations

Heart rate zones: percentage of max HR vs Karvonen

PulseZones offers two ways to calculate heart rate zones. Both use maximum heart rate, but Karvonen also takes resting heart rate into account.

Method 01

Standard method: percentage of max heart rate

The standard method sets zone boundaries as percentages of maximum heart rate. In PulseZones, the lower boundaries of the five zones are 50%, 60%, 70%, 80% and 90%.

Zone boundary = maximum heart rate × percentage

For example, with a maximum heart rate of 180 bpm the 60% mark is: 180 × 0.60 = 108 bpm.

To get started, use your known maximum heart rate or an approximate age-based estimate. PulseZones uses the formula 220 − age.

This calculation is straightforward, but does not account for resting heart rate. Two people with the same maximum will have the same zone boundaries.

Method 02

Karvonen method: heart rate reserve

Heart rate reserve is the difference between maximum and resting heart rate. Karvonen takes a chosen percentage of that difference and adds resting heart rate.

Boundary = resting HR + (maximum HR − resting HR) × percentage

Using the same maximum of 180 bpm and a resting heart rate of 60 bpm, the 60% mark becomes: 60 + (180 − 60) × 0.60 = 132 bpm.

That is 24 beats per minute higher than the previous example. The reason is that 60% of maximum heart rate and 60% of heart rate reserve are different quantities.

What is the idea behind Karvonen, and why use resting heart rate?

Your heart is already working while you rest. During exercise, heart rate rises from that starting point towards its maximum. Karvonen estimates how much of this available range, your heart rate reserve, you are using.

The idea is to measure effort from your resting heart rate rather than from zero. Resting heart rate sets the lower end of your individual scale; maximum heart rate sets the upper end.

The same heart rate, a different share of the reserve

Imagine two people with the same maximum heart rate of 180 bpm. The first has a resting heart rate of 50; the second, 80. Both reach 140 during exercise.

Comparison at a heart rate of 140 bpm
MetricFirst personSecond person
Maximum heart rate180180
Resting heart rate5080
Heart rate reserve130100
Share of reserve at 140 bpm≈ 69%60%
Share of maximum at 140 bpm≈ 78%≈ 78%

The standard method gives both people the same intensity: about 78% of maximum. Karvonen accounts for their different starting points: (140 − 50) ÷ 130 ≈ 69% and (140 − 80) ÷ 100 = 60%. This illustrates the calculation; it does not prove that one person necessarily feels a harder effort.

Why is it more individual, but not always more accurate?

Including resting heart rate relates effort to your available range. Percentage of heart rate reserve generally corresponds more closely to percentage of oxygen uptake reserve than simply assuming that the same percentage of maximum heart rate represents the same relative effort for everyone.

Resting heart rate is influenced by fitness, individual characteristics and your current condition. A lower resting heart rate often accompanies improved endurance, but is not, on its own, a measure of health or fitness.

Which method should you choose?

The standard method is a straightforward starting point. Karvonen gives a more individual guide if you know your usual resting heart rate. Use several calm morning readings, before coffee or activity, rather than a single measurement.

Both methods depend on accurate inputs. If your maximum is estimated using 220 − age, that uncertainty remains with Karvonen too. Neither calculation guarantees that zone boundaries match your individual physiological thresholds.

If you follow a training plan, check both the calculation method and the boundaries in beats per minute. Zone 2 in one app may differ from Zone 2 in another. The number or colour alone is not enough.

Sources: Polar — heart rate reserve and calculation methods; American Society for Preventive Cardiology — exercise intensity.

Frequently asked questions

Before your first workout

Cannot find your answer? Contact the developer. Real user experience helps shape the app.

Which sensors are compatible?

Bluetooth Low Energy sensors with the standard Heart Rate Service. Personally tested: GEOID HS500, Magene H303 and Magene H603.

Does the app work with the screen off?

Yes. Active workouts continue recording in the background. Phones with aggressive power saving may require autostart permission and unrestricted battery use.

Should I pair the sensor in Android settings?

Usually not. Enable Bluetooth and connect the sensor directly in PulseZones.

Are there ads or a paid subscription?

No. PulseZones is free, with no ads or subscription.

Can I use the app as a medical monitor?

No. PulseZones is designed for fitness and workout information. It is not a medical device or a substitute for medical advice.
